summary: GPU provisioning latency in dedicated pool causing batched request stalls and intermittent p99 spikes
description: Issue summary: Several customers on a dedicated pool observed intermittent p99 latency spikes and stalled batched requests between 2026-03-07T22:00Z and 2026-03-08T04:30Z. Impact: production traffic for BlueHarbor Analytics (dedicated) experienced 5-10x p99 increases and occasional 5xx errors when the autoscaler attempted to provision new GPU nodes. Hypothesis: slow GPU node provisioning + KV-cache warming contention from other tenants in same rack causing request batching to stall and queue.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady 50 RPS mixed short/long generation workload pinned to llama-2-13b-q4 on a dedicated pool with burst enabled
2) Force autoscaler to scale up by simulating a sudden 3x traffic surge
3) Observe p99 latency and any increase in request queue depth or 5xx errors
4) Correlate with node provisioning timeline in cloud provider (instance Create/Attach) and with internal scheduler logs
logs: 2026-03-07T22:03:12Z serving-runtime: batch-builder waiting on gpu-alloc for 24ms (expected <5ms)
2026-03-07T22:03:13Z autoscaler: scale-up requested for pool:dedicated-az1 (requested: +2 GPUs)
2026-03-07T22:03:18Z cloud-provider: instance provisioned but network attach delayed 13s
2026-03-07T22:03:31Z gpu-orchestration: driver init took 9s for instance i-0bcd...
2026-03-07T22:03:45Z serving-runtime: KV-cache miss storms observed; cache growth + eviction thrashing on node n-34
2026-03-07T22:03:46Z proxy: 502 from model-worker (health-check failed during warmup)
2026-03-07T22:04:00Z customer-reported: intermittent p99 spikes to 4.2s; baseline p99 ~420ms
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Initial report received from customer at 2026-03-08T01:12Z. Collected timestamps and initial logs. Escalating to infra on-call.

Luis Ortega (SRE): Reproduced a scale-up delay in our staging dedicated pool. Observed node provisioning jitter (6-18s). Noticed KV-cache eviction rate spike when warmup overlaps with heavy small-stream traffic.

Alice Park (Platform Eng): Added hypothesis that our cloud provider network attach latencies are amplifying warmup overlap. Proposing short-term throttle on KV-cache prefetch and introduce backoff for small streams.
Support (to customer): Applied temporary mitigation: reduced burst concurrency on customer pool and enabled conservative autoscale cooldown. Asked customer to monitor for next 6 hours.
Customer (BlueHarbor): Confirmed p99 improved but occasional 2x spikes remain during peak; willing to keep mitigation for further diagnostics.
investigation_notes: 1) Timeline correlation shows autoscaler requested nodes at t=+1s, cloud reported create complete at t=+6-18s depending on AZ. The serving-runtime continued to accept requests, but batch-builder accumulated batches waiting for GPU-alloc leading to queueing and p99 inflation.
2) KV-cache: when new node joins, cache repopulation and small-stream traffic from other tenants caused eviction churn on shared nodes. This made short-context requests slower as prefix cache warmed.
3) Node attach/network delays appear sporadic and correlated with a particular host image (image v2026-02-28). Older images showed longer driver init times.
4) Autoscaler tuning: current aggressive scale-up + immediate traffic routing gives insufficient warmup window for model workers, exposing warmup latency to customers.
5) No evidence of GPU hardware failure; metrics (GPU util, ECC errors) are normal.
6) Related heatmap: p99 spikes align with other tenants' KV prefetch bursts around quarter-hour marks.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-08T05:10Z: temporarily increased autoscaler warmup_delay to 30s for affected dedicated pool and applied per-tenant small-stream concurrency cap (from 80 to 40). This reduced observed p99 for BlueHarbor from 4.2s to ~600ms in the 3-hour window after change.
Short-term fix: rolled back to more conservative node image (v2026-02-20) for pools showing extended driver init times; introduced 5s startup buffer before routing traffic to newly-joined nodes.

Long-term actions: (a) autoscaler change request filed to add staged traffic ramp (RFC #INF-821), (b) kv-cache prefetch backpressure to avoid eviction storms (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2048), (c) cloud image health check and replacement plan to eliminate the slow-init image.
Follow-up: schedule cross-team post-incident review with Platform Eng, Autoscale, and Runtime teams on 2026-03-15. Owner: Luis Ortega.
